stories.summary:
Speculation that Ray Davis could replace the injured Ashton Jeanty



	 



	Ray Davis Could Replace Ashton Jeanty



	 



	SI.com reporter Ezekiel Trezevant reported that Jeanty went down at practice on Sunday, with his teammates apparently fearing a significant injury.



	"During practice, Jeanty landed awkwardly while trying to catch a pass," Trezevant reported. "He stayed down for some time before being helped off the field by trainers, having trouble putting any weight on one leg. As of now, it remains unclear how serious the injury is, but based on his teammates' reaction, it was not good."



	With the season approaching in a few weeks, some NFL analysts suggested the Raiders could hit the trade block for a replacement. Bills reporter and podcaster Bruce Nolan noted that Buffalo's roster has a backup running back looking for a bigger role.



	 



	"Ray Davis said he wanted more playing time," Nolan suggested in response to PFF reporter Nathan Jahnke.



	Davis has proven that he can excel as a lead running back, but his opportunities in Buffalo have been scarce. He took the lead in a 2024 game against the New York Jets with James Cook out with an injury, taking 20 carries for 97 yards and making another three receptions for 55 yards.

Where will Allen end up on all time rushing TD list?
stories.summary:
The running game will continue to be dominant, but I expect less rushing yards and TDs. I think Allen will have a career year in passing TDs, but still pump out anywhere from 8-12 ground scores. When it’s all said & done, he will demolish the rushing TD record for QBs and top 10 all time period. He’s already 23rd all time and HALFWAY thru his career. That is crazy and not talked about enough.
	 



	Jalen Hurts has 63 and is Allen’s closest competition. Both great runners. People tend to dismiss the tush push as easy “gimme” TDs. That’s straight BS. Both QBs have incredible lower body strength. Probably the 2 strongest in the NFL.
	 



	Ask any HOF RB. Those short TDs on the goal line are not a walk in the park. Just so happens Allen is a Mack truck w/ legs. And not are all short yardage. He’s 5th all time in YPC. Another insane feat. 
	 



	I’ll be modest and say Allen will average 7 rushing TDs per year until his retirement at 37 (being modest again.) He’ll have a 2-3 more double digit years and slow down for the remainder as his game progresses into more of a “pocket” QB. 
	 



	So he currently has 79. Add 49 (don’t tell me it isn’t possible, Allen hasn’t lost a step  in speed and QB’s can play much longer) and that puts him at 128 which is 3rd all time behind Emmitt Smith (164) and LT (145.)



	 



	Derrick Henry is still chugging along (122) and will most certainly find his way into the 3rd spot. I give him a 75% shot at surpassing LT and 20% for Emmitt. He’s 32, but has shown zero signs of slowing down coming off a 1500+ 16 TD season. 
	 



	When it’s all said and done, IMO Allen will be top 5 in rushing TDS solidifying himself as the greatest dual threat and perhaps the greatest pure weapon in NFL history.



	 



	What do y’all think? I don’t necessarily want Allen to keep bashing headfirst into a bunch of D-Lineman for the rest of his career, but it would certainly be an awesome accolade to be a top 5 runner and top 15-20 passer of all time. Both very possible. 
	 



	Edit: I know we all want Allen to be less of a focal point in the run game, but it’s pretty tough when u need 1-3 yards at the goal line and not go with the sure thing.

	Since then, he's missed both Pre-Season games, the scrimmage against the Browns, and the Bills 2nd scrimmage practice at the stadium. Which is very important development time for a Rookie.

Winners and Losers Browns Game
stories.summary:
Winners: 



	 



	Kyle Allen- He’s taken a lot of hits on this site this offseason and preseason and through 2 preseason games it has been unwarranted hate. He looked in control and drove the Bills down the field with a balanced attack



	 



	Shane Zylstra- I noticed him last week and again noticed him more this week. He’s been lead blocking, has some soft hands and plays teams. Been around the league but never stuck. Maybe a practice squad guy. 
	 



	Ja’Mori Maclin- Caught two passes including a 71 yard TD pass and another ball down the sideline at the end of the first half to set up the Bills first score from Kyle Allen. 
	 



	Ar’maj Reed Adams- Got the start at Right Guard with the team today and got a ton of reps. Thought he looked very good and has impressed in his two chances. People forget that Adams was a highly thought of prospect before his final season at A&M 



	 



	Da’Metrious Weatherspoon- Got placed at LT early in the 2nd half and didn’t look out of place at all. A huge man with a big wingspan I thought he was the best OT on the field today for the Bills 



	 



	T.J Parker- He is work in progress but unlike last week I felt he affected the game despite getting a sack last week. Better pressure, played the run well. He looked like he was more comfortable. 
	 



	Landon Jackson- Affected the run game and got pressure once in the first half. He’s definitely turning the corner to being at minimum a solid rotational piece with good run stopping abilities 



	 



	Te’Cory Couch- Been on the Bills PS for a bit and he came up with a big interception in the 2nd half on Watson 



	 



	Tommy Doman- Out of his punting efforts all but one of his  punts were good. Solid distance and hang time and buried Cleveland with one of his kicks. 2nd punt was by far his worst 



	 



	Losers: 



	 



	Mecole Hardman- Yes he caught a TD pass but also had a huge drop on a Wide open pass and couldn’t gain separation on another 3rd down that was in his hands before it was ripped out



	 



	Jude Bowry- So they put him at RT this week and in the first drive looked okay then it all started falling apart for him yet again. He doesn’t look pro ready, let alone the swing tackle. 
	 



	Tylan Grable- I’m going to give Grable a bit of a pass because he’s been hurt and hasn’t played Tackle in over a year so I’m sure there was a ton of rust but yuck. He’ll be the Swing Tackle because Bowry isn’t ready but I’m hoping to see a lot more improvement next week. 
	 



	Joe Andreessen- Look if a guy is in front of him as a run stopper he’s not a bad player. He made a lot of nice plays that a LB should make but the man cannot cover at all. He got extremely lucky on the interception and lacks awareness in his drops as a pass defender. 
	 



	Geno Stone- I’ve always liked Stone but he’s been flat out bad through two games here. The Browns picked on him and the other safety who will be named next. He also got beat for the TD last week 



	 



	Damar Hamlin- the dynamic duo of safeties was making me want to gag as the Browns backup WRs just picked apart Stone and Hamlin. At this point I’m all for cutting both of them .

stories.title: Davison Igbinosun: The draft day hate was way overblown
stories.summary:
A lot of folks on here were losing their minds when we drafted Davison Igbinosun, and honestly, the reaction was way overly critical.



	 



	I get where the frustration came from initially. If you watched him at Ohio State, the grabby play and the flags would drive fans batty. But look at the actual body of work—the guy put up great stats, and more importantly, his penalties dropped off dramatically in his final college season once he dialed in the technique.



	 



	Everything we’ve seen out of camp and preseason tells me this kid is a pure competitor. Is he going to get flagged sometimes as a rookie? Probably. Is he going to take some lumps adjusting to NFL receivers? Almost certainly. But what you are getting is pure nastiness, legitimate toughness, and a guy who flat out refuses to back down from anyone. He’s got the ideal physical traits and he’s ridiculously sticky in press-man.



	 



	I mentioned this in another thread, but his real value is going to show up on high-leverage downs. When we dial up a blitz on 3rd-and-medium and the DC needs corners who can get in a receiver's face, disrupt the timing, and hold up on an island for 2.2 seconds to let the rush get home, Igbinosun is built for that exact role.



	 



	Yeah, it's just preseason, but you can't teach that kind of edge. I really like what I'm seeing from him so far.

stories.title: Former 1st round #12 pick Henry Ruggs: 3 to 10 yrs prison for drunk driving fatal crash
stories.summary:
https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38162272/ex-raiders-wr-henry-ruggs-iii-sentenced-3-10-years-fatal-dui



	 



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Ruggs, 24, had been under house arrest with alcohol and location electronic monitoring devices since pleading guilty in May to one count of DUI resulting in death and one count of misdemeanor vehicular manslaughter in the crash that killed Tina Tintor and her dog, Max. On Wednesday, Ruggs read from a statement directed at Tintor's family in which he apologized for his actions.
		

		
			"To the parents and family of Ms. Tintor, I sincerely apologize for the pain and suffering," Ruggs said.
		
	



	 



	Pretty sure Ms Tintor's family don't think 3 years is nearly enough punishment for burning her alive.
	
	Ruggs got what his attorneys asked for:



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			In court documents filed before the sentencing hearing, Ruggs' attorneys had asked the judge to keep the duration of their client's prison time to a range of three to 10 years. Chesnoff and Richard Schonfeld said Ruggs "wishes that he could turn back time and change the outcome of the tragic events of November 2, 2021."
		
	



	 



	I'm sure he does, what with being cut from the team and losing his career and all.  But he can't.
